Now it only makes sense to compare Michigan to other states that test a very high percentage of their students because otherwise you run into selection effect issues (i.e., only college going students take the SAT if it's not required by the state). There are 9 states (including MI) whose participation rate was at least 90% in and 2018 and 2023 (I'm discounting 2021 because SAT wasn't required in MI and 2022 because less than 90% took it in MI).
In terms of the declines in total scale score, MI's decline from 2018 to 2023 was -44 points while the median nationally was -45 points. In other words, MI's declines were about average. for the country DC had the lowest decline (-8 points) and Rhode Island was the highest (-60 points).
MI's standard deviations before in both 2018 and 2023 were also in line with national averages, which suggests the shape of the distribution is similar. But there is a lower mean post-pandemic.

# Troy (MI) School District Updates for Parents & Community Members | The discussion about SAT on the other thread sent me down a rabbit hole that yielded some analysis that others might find interesting | Facebook
Now it only makes sense to compare Michigan to other states that test a very high percentage of their students because otherwise you run into selection effect issues (i.e., only college going students take the SAT if it's not required by the state). There are 9 states (including MI) whose participation rate was at least 90% in and 2018 and 2023 (I'm discounting 2021 because SAT wasn't required in MI and 2022 because less than 90% took it in MI).
In terms of the declines in total scale score, MI's decline from 2018 to 2023 was -44 points while the median nationally was -45 points. In other words, MI's declines were about average. for the country DC had the lowest decline (-8 points) and Rhode Island was the highest (-60 points).
MI's standard deviations before in both 2018 and 2023 were also in line with national averages, which suggests the shape of the distribution is similar. But there is a lower mean post-pandemic.
